module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 325
*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/325](https://www.erdosproblems.com/325)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Asymptotics Filter

namespace Erdos325

/-- A predicate for $n$ to be the sum of three $k$th powers. -/
def IsSumThreePower (k n : ℕ) : Prop := ∃ a b c, a ^ k + b ^ k + c ^ k = n

/-- The number of integers $\leq x$ which are the sum of three $k$th powers. -/
noncomputable def cardIsSumThreePowerBelow (k x : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  {n ∈ Set.Iic x | IsSumThreePower k n}.ncard

/--
Writing $f_{k, 3}(x)$ for the number of integers $\leq x$ which are the sum of three $k$th powers,
is it true that $f_{k, 3}(x) \gg x ^ (3 / k)$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_325 :
     answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k : ℕ, 3 ≤ k → (fun x : ℕ => (x : ℝ) ^ (3 / k : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
      (fun x : ℕ => (cardIsSumThreePowerBelow k x : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
Writing $f_{k, 3}(x)$ for the number of integers $\leq x$ which are the sum of three $k$th powers,
is it even true that $f_{k, 3}(x) \gg_{\epsilon} x ^ (3 / k - \epsilon)$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_325.variants.weaker :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ ε > 0, ∀ k : ℕ, 3 ≤ k → (fun x : ℕ => (x : ℝ) ^ ((3 / k : ℝ) - ε)) =O[atTop]
      (fun x => (cardIsSumThreePowerBelow k x : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
For $k = 3$, the best known is due to Wooley [Wo15], who proved
$f_{3, 3}(x) \gg x^{0.91709477}$.

[Wo15] Wooley, Trevor D., Sums of three cubes, II. Acta Arith. (2015), 73-100.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_325.variants.wooley :
    (fun x : ℕ => (x : ℝ) ^ (0.91709477 : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
      (fun x => (cardIsSumThreePowerBelow 3 x : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos325

reformulations.difference: The counting function and all three asymptotic statements use natural-number cutoffs rather than arbitrary real cutoffs.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For real x ≥ 0, the source's counting function equals cardIsSumThreePowerBelow k ⌊x⌋₊. Since ⌊x⌋₊/x tends to 1, replacing x by its floor preserves each power-law Big-O bound, including negative exponents in the weaker variant. The generic equivalence for every k and real exponent p was proved as natural_cutoff_iff_real_count in /workspace/review/cutoff.lean, without using the file's sorry theorems.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/325 (statement, remarks, and OPEN status, retrieved via https://r.jina.ai/https://www.erdosproblems.com/325)
https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/325 (exact mathematical wording and references, retrieved via https://r.jina.ai/https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/325)
Trevor D. Wooley, Sums of three cubes, II, Acta Arith. 170 (2015), 73–100, Theorem 1.1 and its surrounding discussion; LaTeX source at https://arxiv.org/e-print/1502.01944
https://www.math.purdue.edu/~twooley/publ.html (publication 122, identifying the cited paper and arXiv version)
review.notes: Checked both definitions and all three theorems. The source explicitly requires nonnegative summands and k ≥ 3, matching Lean. The exponents use real division and subtraction, and the Big-O direction gives exactly the requested eventual lower bound with a positive constant; this equivalence was checked in Lean. The counted set is always finite, so Set.ncard's infinite-set default cannot arise. Computable enumeration was proved equivalent to the definition and tested on small inputs, including count(3,0)=1 and count(3,10)=7. Wooley's Theorem 1.1 states the exact exponent 0.91709477. The open/solved categories agree with the sources. Experiments in /workspace/review/scratch.lean and cutoff.lean compile successfully.
